mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in unemployment rate above 5.0% over 3 months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a contraction in consumer demand, reducing corporate revenue growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or interaction term Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) signals manufacturing output contraction that reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth rises, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% signals persistent inflationary pressures, prompting Federal Reserve tightening that reduces equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous CPI inflation increases (CPIAUCSL) and industrial production declines (INDPRO) indicate stagflation, reducing corporate profitability and investor confidence, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises and INDPRO falls, or interaction term Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing GDP growth (GDPC1) signals late-cycle economic deceleration where corporate earnings growth weakens, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth slows, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
